text.p: Eastman Kodak Co. said Tuesday its earnings fell in the first quarter as sales were hit by the stronger dollar, and the photographic and imaging products company called the results unsatisfactory.

"Overall, 1997 started more slowly than we expected and the first quarter results are unsatisfactory," Kodak Chairman George Fisher said in a statement. "We need to improve our execution to achieve results which reflect the company's true potential."

First quarter net earnings were $149 million, or 45 cents per share, which included a pre-tax charge of $186 million for in-process research and development related to the company's acquisition of the software business unit of Wang Laboratories.

Excluding the acquisition-related charge, earnings were $272 million in the first quarter compared with $274 million a year ago. Operating earnings per share, however, rose to 82 cents from 80 cents with fewer shares outstanding this year.
Sales fell to $3.13 billion from $3.39 billion.
"Without the adverse effect of foreign currency, sales would have increased by 5 percent," it said. A stronger dollar makes overseas sales worth less in dollar terms.
Total sales also were hurt by flat sales in emerging markets, and lower prices. But Kodak said it believed emerging markets will be a source of long-term growth in the future.
Consumer imaging sales were $1.5 billion in the quarter, up 3 percent from a year ago, while commercial imaging sales were down 16 percent to $1.64 billion.
Eastman Kodak stock rose $2.25 to $75.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
